title: Audit Defence and Controversy

sections.body: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of responding to a tax authority's questions, from the first information request through formal dispute and, where it applies, litigation or competent authority proceedings. It sits inside tax and jurisdictional compliance because the same transaction can be examined by more than one revenue body under different rules. The subject includes penalty exposure, interest computations, documentation requests, and the internal record that shows how a position was taken and maintained.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on the company's tax provision and return files, the general ledger, transfer pricing documentation, contracts, and correspondence with the revenue body. Practitioners typically work in tax controversy or dispute resolution systems, document management platforms, and spreadsheets or databases that reconcile the numbers under challenge. Increasingly the underlying data sits in ERP and e-invoicing systems, so access and version control matter as much as the analysis itself.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method is evidence led. A controversy team reconstructs the facts, maps each disputed item to the statute or treaty provision relied on, and builds a response that is consistent with positions taken in other years and other jurisdictions. Responses are drafted, reviewed by internal tax and often external advisers, and filed within statutory deadlines. Where the dispute continues, the file moves to appeals, mutual agreement, or advance pricing mechanisms, and the same factual record is reused.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on privilege, confidentiality, and the duty to disclose accurately. Documents prepared for the purpose of obtaining legal advice may attract privilege in some jurisdictions but not others, and penalties can follow careless or unsupported positions. Provenance matters because a defence rests on the contemporaneous record, so retention policies, legal hold, and audit trails for any automated analysis need to be in place before a query arrives. This site tracks 229 compliance and regulation pages and 150 active AI lawsuits, which shows how often these questions end up contested.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Revenue bodies are expanding their use of data analytics and country by country reporting, which shortens the gap between filing and query and widens the number of items examined. That pushes controversy teams toward earlier documentation, more standardised evidence packs, and closer coordination between tax, legal, and finance. The direction is toward continuous readiness rather than a scramble when a notice arrives, with the same data used for provision, return, and defence.
